children: Ford Motor Company (NYSE:F) is betting big on EVs—pricing the Fathom pickup near $30,000, opening orders next year and targeting 100,000+ U.S. units—while navigating softer U.S. sales, a major recall, labor and legal fallout, bond-market interest and lobbying on China-made cars.
Ford Motor Company Fathom EV Price Near 30000
: Ford (F) will price the Fathom EV pickup near $30,000, open orders early next year, build it on a new Louisville assembly line, and targets 100,000+ U.S. units in year one
Ford August Sales Down, EV Down
: Ford (F) August U.S. sales 170,681 units, down 10.3% YoY. YTD through August 1.35M units, down 9.8%. EV sales 144,316 YTD, down 32.2%. August SUV sales -23.3%, cars +12.7%, trucks ~-1%.
: Ford (F) recalls about 158,664–159,000 U.S. vehicles for defects causing sudden loss of drive power and headlight/windshield-washer malfunctions; NHTSA says issues may raise crash risk.
: Ford (F) has a 6% subordinated baby bond (F.PRC) maturing 2059, trading near $20 and yielding ~7.7% to maturity; rated BBB-/Ba1. Key data for traders: yield, price, maturity, credit grade.
: Ford (F) backed a coalition urging Congress to ban Chinese-made passenger cars in the U.S. by year-end, citing subsidized models with connected hardware/software as a national security risk.
: Ford (F) will pay $2.3M to settle an EEOC probe into racist graffiti at its Buffalo stamping plant, must run anti-discrimination training for three years and report complaints to the EEOC.
